About this demo

Every route and preference calculation uses Brisbane City Council data. The base map is supplied by OpenStreetMap for display only and is never read by the routing algorithm.

Routes connect shared vertices in BCC Bikeway sections and the LGIP Existing Bikeway dataset. No missing connection is drawn. This planning graph does not contain current closures, legal direction or turning restrictions and is not a turn-by-turn navigation service.

Arrivals are nearby BCC cycleway nodes, not building entrances. Three preference modes can select the same path when the data favours it.

Protected bikeways uses mapped off-road length as a proxy; physical barriers are not verified. Traffic is a saved BCC signal-flow snapshot from 15 Sep 2026, not live traffic. Hills use terrain estimates from 2002 contours; bridge decks and tunnels are excluded. Check each route’s coverage.

Hazards are explicitly labelled sample scenarios or your local reports. They do not affect BCC route calculations. Ride movement is simulated; no GPS is used.

BCC Bikeway sections · BCC Existing Bikeway · BCC Intersection volume · BCC Intersection locations · BCC Contours 2002

AI Use Declaration

This application was developed with assistance from ChatGPT and Codex. The team reviewed, adapted and tested AI-assisted outputs before incorporating them into the project.

BCC Data presentation slide

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Here is the content for our BCC Data slide. Suggest a simple visual layout for the slide.”

How it was used: ChatGPT was asked to suggest a visual layout using content provided by the team.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested layout was adapted for the BCC Data presentation slide. All written content, technical information and data sources were provided and checked by the team.

Presentation script editing

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Check my presentation script, fix the grammar and make any unclear wording sound more natural.”

How it was used: ChatGPT was used to correct grammatical errors and improve unclear or inappropriate wording.

Validation and incorporation: The revised wording was used in the final presentation script. The original content and technical information were provided and checked by the team.

Git branch and merge guidance

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Show me step by step how to create and switch branches, add and commit files, push my changes, and merge my work using Git.”

How it was used: ChatGPT provided step-by-step guidance on creating and switching branches, adding and committing files, pushing changes and merging team members’ work.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance was used to manage individual Git branches and integrate the prototype files. Team members executed the commands and checked the repository after each operation.

Leaflet map troubleshooting

Tool: ChatGPT / Codex

Example prompt: “The Leaflet map is not displaying correctly. Here are the relevant HTML and JavaScript files and a screenshot of the problem. Help me identify the possible causes and suggest how to test them.”

How it was used: ChatGPT and Codex were used to diagnose technical problems in the prototype using the code, screenshots and error information supplied by the team.

Validation and incorporation: The team selected and applied the relevant fixes, then checked that the map and its related interactions worked correctly.

BCC data processing and route calculation

Tool: ChatGPT / Codex

Example prompt: “Using these BCC bikeway datasets, help us process the data into a connected cycling network and calculate route options based on distance and route preferences.”

How it was used: AI assisted with designing and implementing the workflow that processes BCC bikeway data into a connected network and calculates route options. The team supplied the selected datasets, route requirements and expected behaviours.

Validation and incorporation: The output was adapted into the data-processing scripts and route calculation module. The team reviewed the code, tested the routes on the map, corrected unrealistic connections and checked that the results matched the project requirements and data limitations.

WIP feedback transcription

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Please transcribe this recording of the feedback from our WIP demonstration.”

How it was used: ChatGPT was used to transcribe an audio recording of the feedback received during the WIP demonstration. The transcript was checked against the recording, corrected and organised into key issues and further details.

Validation and incorporation: The transcript was used to summarise the WIP feedback and plan future improvements to the prototype. The team reviewed the output before using it in the feedback document.

JavaScript interface implementation and debugging

Tool: Claude

Example prompt: “Help us implement and debug the JavaScript interface functionality in this prototype.”

How it was used: Claude was used to help solve technical issues, mainly when implementing and debugging interface functionality in JavaScript.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested changes were reviewed and applied to the relevant JavaScript files. The resulting interface behaviour was then tested manually in the prototype.

Locating the destination-selection code

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Help me find which code controls destination selection and which files I need to modify.”

How it was used: ChatGPT provided guidance on locating the code responsible for destination selection and identifying the files that needed to be modified.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance was used to identify the relevant planner code before making changes. The existing project structure and behaviour were checked before editing.

Improving the destination-selection interaction

Tool: Claude

Example prompt: “Help me change the destination-selection interaction so that selecting one destination highlights it without hiding the other available destinations.”

How it was used: Claude provided coding guidance for improving the destination-selection interaction.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested approach informed changes to the destination-selection logic in the planner. The interaction was tested in the prototype to confirm that users could still view and switch between destinations.

Interpreting the route-planning interface

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Help me understand the implemented route-planning interface, including route preferences, generated route options and the ‘Same path’ result.”

How it was used: ChatGPT was used to explain the difference between route preferences, generated route options and the “Same path” result.

Validation and incorporation: The explanation was used to check that the interface and presentation accurately described the implemented route-planning behaviour. No route calculation results were generated by ChatGPT.

Integrating the destination update with Git

Tool: ChatGPT / Codex

Example prompt: “Show me how to add the relevant modified file, write a commit message and push this destination-interaction update using Git.”

How it was used: ChatGPT and Codex provided guidance on selecting the relevant modified file, writing a commit message and pushing the change.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance supported the Git workflow used to integrate the destination interaction update into the team repository.

Debugging disappearing destination options

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Review this destination-selection code and help identify why the other destination options disappear after one is selected.”

How it was used: ChatGPT was used to review the destination-selection code and identify the cause of the disappearing options.

Validation and incorporation: The explanation was used to understand the existing selection behaviour and guide the modification. The final behaviour was verified manually in the website.
